reviews.text:
⭐☆☆☆☆ 1 STAR — Art Workout is NOT worth £60 a month!

Honestly, I was drawing on Art Workout, and halfway through, I didn’t even want to draw anymore. It completely drained my energy, and afterwards, I didn’t feel like I could do any more drawing. 💀 How is a drawing app supposed to make drawing feel like a chore instead of something fun?!

AND THE PRICE?! 😭 I am NOT paying £60 a month for a GAME. SIXTY QUID?! Be so fr right now. That’s ridiculous for an app that’s supposed to be enjoyable. Drawing is meant to be relaxing, not something that leaves you exhausted and makes you not want to pick up your Apple Pencil again.

It shouldn’t feel like I’m paying a fortune just to draw some pictures. There should be more affordable options, and people shouldn’t feel pressured to pay that much just to enjoy the app.

Overall, I’m disappointed. It has potential, but the experience and the price make it not worth it for me. Art Workout, please get it together, because my wallet is NOT fighting for its life over a drawing game. 💀😭

reviews.title: Not good
reviews.text: Actually, I had downloaded this app before. However, I hadn't really explored it much. I deleted it right away because of the energy shortage issue. Now, seeing it again and checking the reviews, I thought I'd give it another chance. But I regret it. This app appears to be free, but it definitely isn't. The ads are beyond being just a problem. At the same time, if you are using it for free, you are supposed to get energy once every 24 hours. They create the impression that you can practice once a day, but that's not how it works either. They don't actually give you any energy. If you watch 3 long ads, they give you one energy. If you don't watch them, you get nothing. So, they don't even give you a chance to try the app and see whether you like it or not. It would make more sense if the app were offered as a paid one directly. I also looked at the reviews. There are constant complaints about ads, and they've replied to everyone, thanking them and saying they will forward the feedback. But when I examine the recent update notes for the app, no changes have been made. In other words, there is actually no attempt showing they intend to fix this situation. It's almost as if they have an attitude of "use it if you want, don't use it if you don't."

reviews.title: Horrible business practices, but good selection
reviews.text:
I’ll give this two stars because the options are good, but the horrible ad system and scam-like operation of this app is unbearable. I get that there needs to be ads in a free version, but ArtWorkout tries to annoy you so badly with ads in an attempt to make you buy their subscription.

They present their subscription as a forced ad over and over, and normally you just wait 30 seconds or so for the ads to pass, but this app forces you to click “view all plans" repeatedly and you have to click a faded out “decline” button. If that was it, fine, but to start any picture, they make you use 1 energy. To get ONE energy you have to go through 3 ads (including the one I mentioned above where you have to click thru and decline subscriptions).

reviews.title: Zero Accessibility Features
reviews.text:
I’ve been using this app for almost 2 months now as a paid user. I paid for a year subscription.
There are lots of cute guided drawings in this app, but there are absolutely no accessibility features. Dark mode isn’t compatible with this app like it is other similar art apps, and devs have no plans to add it, as one of the devs said “you can’t draw black on black” to me when I requested it. But there are several lessons in this app where you have to draw white on white. I requested this feature as a toggle for those of us with vision problems & eye strain. Another user agreed with me, and a dev told them that they probably just “have a cheap iPad”. Also, there are no stabilization features for users who suffer from tremors or just generally have shaky hands, again with no plans to add it. A developer told a user who requested it that they “can’t cater to everyone“. 

Apps like this that are advertised as “meditation tools” and “recovery and healing through art” should absolutely not be lacking in accessibility features, and the way the dev team speaks to users who request them is honestly disgusting. Specifically “Sasha from ArtWorkout” in the official discord server for this app. 

All this being said, I gave the app a fair chance, and there are a lot of cute things about this app. But the negatives outweigh the positives for me here. No accessibility features at all - with no plans to add them. 

I wouldn’t continue to use this app if they paid me.

reviews.title: Too many things need the membership 😕
reviews.text: Overall I think this is a good app, I enjoy coming onto it when I need to relax and draw something without having to think too much. But it can be a bit annoying when you’re trying to use the app without paying. You need the membership for almost everything, and as an app that’s advertised as free, I don’t like that. You can only do one lesson a day, after watching an ad to get energy, then you’re cut off for the day. I opened the app today only to notice that most of the lessons aren’t available anymore, and you needed the membership to use the eraser. In a word, it’s frustrating. I know the app has to make money, but really? Make it more accessible for people who don’t want to pay, are too young to pay for it themselves, or just make the app cost money in the first place. Let the user watch an ad before each lesson, or watch an ad to get energy multiple times. I feel cheated, please advertise the app as it is.
